install_tell: SaaS guardrail API for LLM/agent applications (prompt-injection, jailbreak, data-exfil detection). Deployed on AWS EKS behind an ingress controller; origin not directly reachable. Auth fronted by PropelAuth (managed B2B auth) at the edge. No exposed data plane.
misconfig_patterns: Host-header probe to EKS origin returns ingress default-backend, not app -- no exposure
TLS SNI mismatch surfaces 'Kubernetes Ingress Controller Fake Certificate' / ingress.local (default-backend tell, not a finding)

passive: EKS ingress default-backend on SNI miss (Fake Certificate / ingress.local)
PropelAuth edge redirect on auth paths

response_markers: Kubernetes Ingress Controller Fake Certificate (default-backend on SNI/Host miss)
active_probe.false_positive_check: default-backend 404 / fake-cert is NOT a finding; require correct Host + authenticated JSON read for any exposure claim

deployment_tells: AWS EKS ingress controller; origin hidden behind default-backend on Host/SNI mismatch
PropelAuth managed auth at the edge (B2B SSO)
No raw data-plane endpoint exposed in cert-pivot sweep
pivot_paths: PropelAuth tenant enumeration (edge auth, no backend leak observed)
category_lane_classification: Lane B (policy / prompt-injection defense for agent actions).
